en: The Sūtra on the Merit of Circumambulating a Buddha Stūpa,
translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Śikṣānanda and others of the Kingdom of Khotan during the Great Zhou Dynasty, by imperial decree.
Thus have I heard:
At one time, the Buddha was staying at Śrāvastī in the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍada’s Park, together with a great assembly of bhikṣus and countless other followers, who surrounded him on all sides.
At that time, the Elder Śāriputra rose from his seat, bared his right shoulder, knelt with his right knee on the ground, joined his palms toward the Buddha, and requested him in verse:
“O World-Honored One of Great Majestic Virtue,
We pray that you will explain for our sake The fruit and retribution obtained By circumambulating a Buddha-stūpa to the right.”
At that time, the World-Honored One answered in verse:
"The various merits obtained by circumambulating a Buddha-stūpa—now I shall speak of but a small portion thereof; all of you listen well."
All devas, nāgas, yakṣas, spirits, and the like, will all draw near and make offerings;
this is due to circumambulating the stūpa to the right.
In whatever place they are born, they will remain far removed from the eight difficulties.
One is always born in places free from calamity; this is due to circumambulating a stūpa clockwise.
In every place of birth, mindfulness and wisdom are never lost;
one is endowed with exquisite physical marks; this is due to circumambulating a stūpa clockwise.
Coming and going among devas and humans, their merit and lifespan shall both be long and far-reaching;
they will always obtain great renown—this is due to circumambulating the stūpa to the right.
Dwelling in Jambudvīpa, they will always be born as the most honored and supreme.
Born into a pure lineage, this results from circumambulating the stūpa clockwise.
One’s appearance is always upright and handsome, and one possesses great wealth and treasures;
constantly enjoying vast fiefdoms, this results from circumambulating the stūpa clockwise.
Wealth and treasures are always abundant, yet one is free from avarice;
with courage and vigor, one practices extensive giving—this is due to circumambulating the stūpa clockwise.
One’s physical appearance becomes pure and sublime, such that all who see it feel joy and admiration.
One’s dwelling is always peaceful and blissful; this results from circumambulating a stūpa clockwise.
Or one becomes a king of the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven, with wife and children all complete, possessing sovereign power and authority;
this results from circumambulating a stūpa clockwise.
Some become brahmins, who maintain the precepts and are well-versed in incantations and the Vedas;
this results from circumambulating the stupa to the right.
Others become great elders, noble and wealthy with abundant property.
The granaries are always full and abundant; this results from circumambulating the stupa to the right.
One may become a sovereign of the True Dharma, a king who rules over Jambudvīpa with mastery, and all the lands submit to his transformation;
this results from circumambulating the stupa to the right.
Some become wheel-turning kings of great power, possessing the seven treasures, who govern all living beings through the ten wholesome deeds;
this results from circumambulating the stūpa to the right.
From this they are born in the heavens, always possessing great majesty and virtue.
Pure faith in the Buddha’s Dharma arises from circumambulating the stūpa clockwise.
Once pure faith is swiftly perfected, one will have no delusions regarding the Dharma;
seeing that all conditioned phenomena are empty arises from circumambulating the stūpa clockwise.
Passing away from the celestial realm, He descends to be born among humans;
Entering the womb without confusion— This results from circumambulating the stupa to the right.
While dwelling within the mother’s womb, He remains unsullied by any impurity.
Like a pure maṇi jewel, this results from circumambulating the stūpa to the right.
While in the womb and at the time of birth, it causes the mother to be ever peaceful and happy;
even while nursing, it is likewise so—this results from circumambulating the stūpa to the right.
Parents and kinsmen, all together nourish and raise them;
a wet nurse is never absent—this is due to circumambulating the stupa to the right.
Their retinue will love and cherish them even more than their own parents.
One's wealth and resources increase of their own accord; this is due to circumambulating the stūpa clockwise.
Yakṣas and various malevolent spirits cannot cause even a moment’s alarm or fear;
one obtains whatever is needed spontaneously; this is due to circumambulating the stūpa clockwise.
After passing through hundreds of thousands of kalpas, his body becomes increasingly pure, and his wondrous physical marks reach full perfection; this is due to circumambulating the stupa.
His pure eyes are long and wide, resembling the blue lotus flower.
Furthermore, one attains the pure divine eye, This results from circumambulating the stūpa to the right.
Exquisite form is ever-perfect, Adorned naturally with all the marks;
One achieves great power and influence, This results from circumambulating the stūpa to the right.
Some are born in the palace of Śakra, possessing great majesty and sovereignty as the honored one among the Trāyastriṃśa devas; this results from circumambulating a stūpa clockwise.
Others are born in the palaces of Suyāma or Tuṣita.
Born among the Nirmāṇarati and Paranirmita-vaśavartin devas, this results from circumambulating the stūpa clockwise.
Or else one is born in the Brahmā heavens, attaining supreme sovereignty in the Brahma-world and being constantly honored by all the devas;
this results from circumambulating the stūpa clockwise.
For billions of nayutas of kalpas, they shall always be revered and honored by all wise people;
this is due to their circumambulating stupas to the right.
Their bodies and their garments shall remain forever stainless for billions of kalpas.
To be fully endowed with pure and white dharmas is due to circumambulating the stūpa to the right.
To possess the power of great diligence, to assiduously cultivate various practices without ever succumbing to weariness or indolence,
is due to circumambulating the stūpa to the right.
Courageous and ever-diligent, firm and indestructible, one swiftly accomplishes all that is undertaken;
this is due to circumambulating the stūpa to the right.
With a profound and subtle voice, all who hear it are filled with joy.
Peace and happiness, and being forever free from illness—these arise from circumambulating the stūpa clockwise.
As I have proclaimed: the wearying abandonment of the suffering of the three realms of existence and the accomplishment of supramundane wisdom—these arise from circumambulating the stūpa clockwise.
They constantly abide in the four foundations of mindfulness, as well as the four right efforts and the four bases of psychic power;
all this arises from circumambulating the stupa clockwise.
They thoroughly realize the four noble truths, the faculties, the powers, and the seven factors of enlightenment.
The right path and the noble fruits— these arise from circumambulating the stūpa clockwise.
The extinction of all afflictions, the possession of great majestic power,
and the six untainted supernormal knowledges— these arise from circumambulating the stūpa clockwise.
Forever free from greed, hatred, and delusion, as well as all hindrances, one realizes the enlightenment of a Pratyekabuddha;
this is due to circumambulating a stūpa to the right.
One attains a wondrous golden-hued body, adorned with the marks and signs of excellence,
appearing as a Teacher of Gods and Humans— all this results from circumambulating stupas clockwise.
All of this arises from bodily actions and verbal praise.
By circumambulating a Buddha stūpa, one obtains this great benefit.
Regarding the various merits gained from circumambulating the stūpas of all Buddhas,
how could I possibly exhaustively describe them now, even by briefly recounting what I have heard?
When the World-Honored One had spoken these verses, Śāriputra and the entire assembly were all greatly rejoiced; they believed, accepted, and practiced them accordingly.
*The Sūtra on the Merit of Circumambulating a Buddha-Stūpa*.
